children: Crude oil climbed toward $95 per barrel on Wednesday, marking its fifth consecutive session of gains as escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthi rebels intensified concerns over Middle East supply disruptions.
On Tuesday, Yemen’s Houthi militants struck Saudi Aramco’s headquarters in Dhahran, eastern Saudi Arabia, with a missile attack that sparked a fire in part of the complex.
The rebels also targeted Riyadh’s main airport over the weekend, while a Saudi-led coalition launched an offensive to retake rebel-controlled territory in Yemen.

Meanwhile, Tehran has intensified attacks on tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz, although the US said it had helped facilitate the passage of more than 19 million barrels of crude through the strategic waterway.
In Europe, President Trump defended his diesel export agreement with Russia, stating that the additional supplies would enter the global market and help ease elevated prices.

title: Oil Extends Gains on Mideast Escalations
